about.title: Auburn Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Auburn is a small city, and a sudden loss here is felt well beyond one household. In 2025, the city recorded 52 injury collisions and 70 people hurt, with no traffic deaths reported that year, a reminder that most families in Auburn will never face this. Some still do, whether from a crash on I-80, Grass Valley Highway, Auburn Folsom Road or Route 49, or from a fall, a workplace incident, or a medical error. California law gives certain survivors the right to bring a civil wrongful death claim. A surviving spouse or domestic partner and children have first standing, followed by specific dependents and heirs. The claim is separate from any criminal case, and it does not depend on one. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it can be much shorter when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Auburn families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Auburn Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Questions Answered Early
items.desc: California limits who can file, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you are connected with can sort out who belongs in the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines Tracked From Day One
items.desc: Two years from the date of death is the usual limit, but a claim against a city, county or state agency must be presented far sooner. Getting connected promptly helps protect that window.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery

items.question: My loved one died in a crash on I-80 near Auburn. Does it matter that no criminal charges were filed?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action with its own standard of proof, and it can proceed whether or not a prosecutor brings charges. The attorney you are connected with can gather the CHP or Auburn Police report, witness accounts and other evidence on its own track.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children have the first right to file. If there are none, certain financially dependent relatives and other heirs may qualify. An attorney can review your family's situation to confirm who has standing.

items.question: What can our family actually recover?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have contributed, and the loss of love, companionship, comfort and guidance. Each category is evaluated separately, and no attorney can promise a particular result. What matters first is preserving the claim before the two-year deadline, or the shorter one that applies to public entities.
